parsed.note_markdown:
### KEY — Strong spread growth and improving credit

**Reported GAAP diluted EPS increased to $0.51 from $0.44 in 2Q26**, a $0.07 sequential improvement. Net income available to common shareholders totaled $537 million, up from $473 million. Reported and adjusted EPS were identical, with no selected-item EPS adjustment [B0350, B0357, B0521, B0522].

**Revenue and margin:** GAAP NII grew $50 million to $1,300 million, with taxable-equivalent NIM expanding 6 basis points to 2.95%. Noninterest income rose to $744 million from $706 million, while expenses increased to $1,245 million from $1,217 million [B0043, B0035, B0044, B0086]. The reported cash efficiency ratio was 60.6% [B0368].

**Credit:** Provision declined from $92 million to $61 million, and net charge-offs decreased from $115 million to $89 million. The annualized charge-off ratio improved to 0.32%, with ACL coverage of 1.50% [B0127, B0118, B0119, B0126].

**Capital and returns:** CET1 was 11.1%; ROTCE reached 15.11%; tangible book value was $12.35 per share. Share repurchases totaled $320 million [B0138, B0032, B0360, B0157].

**Outlook:** Management indicated approximately 10% full-year NII growth, approximately 5% average loan growth, a fourth-quarter NIM exit target near 3.00%, and a lower 37–39 basis-point charge-off expectation versus the previous 40–45 basis-point range [B1017].

**Investment thesis:** Positive incremental development. Stronger NIM, earnings growth and an improved credit outlook reinforce the recovery narrative, though expense growth and tangible book value remain important considerations.
